newsitem.title: USA: CSCE coffee called to open 4.00 cents higher.
newsitem.headline: CSCE coffee called to open 4.00 cents higher.

text.p: CSCE coffee futures were called to open 4.00 cents per lb higher on Thursday, after the London robusta market fell well short of pre-opening expectations, traders said.
Prices in London were due to open $200 lower on Thursday, but gapped just $85 lower and by the midday break were just $35 to $65 easier. Benchmark LIFFE September was down $50, to $1,815.

But some New York traders said follow-through selling after Wednesday's finish near session lows could pressure the market, with operators attempting to find sell-stops in the CSCE September contract below the 175.00-cent level, a double bottom on the charts.

Wednesday, New York arabica futures fell sharply, as chart-driven speculative selling drove September to an eight-week low. September dropped 15.15 cents, to 175.50, after ranging from 193.50 to 175.00. Spot July fell 18.65 cents, to 190.05, while the outer months closed 8.65 to 12.15.
The July/September switch shrunk to 14.50 cents at the close, from 18.00 cents on Tuesday.
Some traders said the lack of a build in exchange-certified coffee stocks heading into the July delivery period on Friday could underpin the market.
After Wednesday's close, CSCE reported certified coffee stocks fell by 264 bags as of June 17, to 47,286 bags. There were 1,500 bags pending grading, the exchange said.
On the weather front, no damaging cold is indicated over the next seven days in Brazil's coffee belt, U.S.-based forecaster Weather Services Corp said on Thursday.
